conventions.convention: The function codomain is R union {+∞}, with no −∞ values; properness requires nonempty effective domain. Convex combinations use 0·(+∞)=0. Lower semicontinuity means every real weak sublevel set is closed; epigraph heights are real.
The conjugate supremum ranges over dom f; the biconjugate supremum ranges over finite conjugate values and uses sup ∅=−∞. The subdifferential is empty outside dom f.
Separation has orientation ⟨u,e⟩ ≤ c < ⟨u,z⟩ for all e in the nonempty closed convex set, with u nonzero.
Coercivity of the fixed tilt g means that for every real M some R>0 makes ||x||≥R imply g(x)>M. Extended-real values are permitted, and attainment does not imply uniqueness.

Mixtures use a nonempty finite list of finite data, nonnegative weights summing to one, and value +∞ outside their convex hull. The supporting-face assertion assumes an existing subgradient and applies to every positive-weight constituent of any minimizing mixture.
The ordered-mixture transfer assumes the strict-reference draft representation conclusion, distinct state labels, and the specified affine coordinate assignment; it asserts no physical adoption.

Concave supporting bounds require only the explicitly admitted segments. Global affine-slice maximality requires stationarity on ker A and concavity along every segment from the candidate to a feasible point. Hessian semidefiniteness does not imply strict curvature.

The curvature test uses a continuous symmetric matrix field representing all second directional derivatives and stationarity on ker A. Zero-dimensional ambient spaces and ker A={0} are handled explicitly; strict minimality on a singleton is vacuous.

The tangent cone uses positive times tending to zero and convergent perturbed directions. Active zero-amount species require (νh)j≥0. Extents and species amounts share a fixed amount unit; ν is dimensionless.
The rank theorem requires 1≤q≤n and a specified invertible q-by-q derivative minor. It gives a C1 graph for q<n and an isolated zero for q=n; a singleton has local graph dimension zero.

Phase coordinates use positive T,p and interior compositions, with R0={0} and Ω1={0}. Dimension counts require the stated nonsingular minors; they make no assertion at singular solutions or composition boundaries.

load_bearing.statement: For a C1 map F:U⊆Rⁿ→Rᵠ, 1≤q≤n, with F(x*)=0 and an invertible q-by-q derivative minor, the local zero set is, after coordinate permutation, a unique C1 graph over n−q coordinates when q<n, with Dφ=−(DvF)⁻¹DuF. When q=n, the zero is locally isolated.
Let d≥1 and let f:Rᵈ→R∪{+∞} be closed, proper, and convex in the stated conventions. Then f**(x)=f(x) for every x∈Rᵈ.
Let n≥1, let E⊆Rⁿ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let z∉E. Then there are nonzero u∈Rⁿ and real c such that ⟨u,e⟩≤c<⟨u,z⟩ for every e∈E.
For proper f, x∈dom f, and p∈Rᵈ, f*(p)≥⟨p,x⟩−f(x), with equality exactly when p∈∂f(x), equivalently when x attains the conjugate supremum; that supremum is then finite.

For finite data q1,…,qm∈Rᵈ and a1,…,am∈R, with m,d≥1, the minimum weighted value at fixed barycenter is attained, extends by +∞ outside the convex hull to a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function, and is greatest among convex functions h satisfying h(qi)≤ai. It equals its biconjugate. If p∈∂f_mix(x), every positive-weight constituent of any minimizing mixture satisfies ai=⟨p,qi⟩−f_mix*(p).

Differentiability and the displayed concavity inequality on an admitted segment imply f(y)≤f(x)+Df(x)(y−x). Stationarity on ker A gives global maximality on the affine feasible slice under the stated segment hypotheses; strict concavity on a convex feasible slice gives uniqueness. For C2 f, the stated local midpoint inequality implies D²f(x)[h,h]≤0 for every h.

For F={ξ:n0+νξ≥0}, the Bouligand tangent cone at ξ* is exactly {h:(νh)j≥0 for every active species j}. A differentiable relative local minimum has Df(ξ*)h≥0 on this cone; for a convex differentiable objective on a convex open domain this is sufficient for global minimality on F∩U. Under the stated composition hypotheses, Df(ξ*)h=(νᵀμ)·h.
